answer: A DKG-based beacon derives randomness from a distributed key generation ceremony, and the pearl of the design is that the beacon key is shared so no single party controls the output. The island of the protocol is that each beacon round is a threshold signature on the round number, which anyone can verify. A Sybil cannot predict or influence the beacon because it needs a quorum to sign, and the jetty of the beacon gives every applicant a fair, unpredictable verifier assignment.
